message.content: {"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"0","derivation":"Retained unchanged from the R1 source-only construction. Local operation at u=0: with g = r/2 + r^2*B(r,0) and B = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2), one verifies g = sqrt(1+r)-1 (the rationalized small root), so (1+g)^2 = 1+r = p and the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r vanishes identically. The whole residual E = (2g+g^2-r) + 2ug retains the cross term 2ug = O(ur) for u != 0; this is the documented limitation of the source-published u=0 construction and is not a defect of the coefficient body. Smoothness: sqrt(1+r) is C-infinity for r > -1; chi_r support is |r| <= 1/2 giving 1+r >= 1/2 > 0 throughout the evaluation rectangle, so B extends smoothly to an open neighborhood of the closed rectangle [-1/2,1/2] x [-1/4,1/4]. C=0 retains the published source choice. The analytic certificate (ANALYTIC_ON_CORE_NEIGHBORHOOD, CONDITIONAL_SMOOTH_FAMILY) confirms the domain. Numerical feedback from stage 1: all in-support rows report residuals at machine-precision level (|residual| <= 1.8e-71 for UNIFORM rows where the cross term is negligible; O(ur) residuals for rows with larger u). No NO_APPLIED_UPDATE failures. The OUT-of-support row (LEFT:t=1/64:x=1/8:s=0, r=-1, chi_r=0) correctly falls back to g=r/2 with residual 0.25, as designed. This is a local coefficient identity within the NS source family, not a PDE estimate or global NS proof.","inspect":[],"note":"Retained at generation 2. Successor considerations: (1) After stage 1, z_after != 1 at most non-ZERO points, so u = z_after - 1 is nonzero at the next stage. The whole residual will include 2ug = O(ur); for the UNIFORM family this is ~1e-8 to 1e-7 (u~0.008-0.014, g~1e-6), well within tolerance. For the LEFT/RIGHT/BOTH families with larger u (up to ~0.5), the cross term can be O(1e-4) and is the dominant residual; this is expected behavior, not a failure. (2) If a future stage drives r below -1 before chi_r fades to zero (|r| > 1/2), sqrt(1+r) would hit a negative argument and the program becomes unusable at that point (NO_APPLIED_UPDATE, z unchanged). Current targets with tau=1/64 or 1/128 keep r well within [-1, 0.0625]. (3) C=0 is the source-published choice; a nonzero C (e.g. C=-1/2) could cancel the leading O(ur) cross term but would couple the slots and is outside the R1 construction. Retain unless successor feedback shows the cross term dominates the stability budget at multiple points simultaneously. (4) The ZERO family remains z=1.0 exactly by construction (p=1, r=0, g=0); no correction is applied. (5) The chi_u gating (|u|<=1/8 full, |u|>=1/4 zero) correctly suppresses the nonlinear correction where u is large; points with |u|>1/4 receive only the linear r/2 increment. (6) The archived finite-root expressions remain valid for their original finite-task scope; this smooth body is the field-stage coefficient operator."}
